title: The coach writes an eating plan, recorded
desc: A recorded Claude Code session with a made-up athlete: /fitness-coach diet screens first, asks how much to count and what a normal day looks like, then proposes an eating plan built around the athlete's own meals, with its sources.
window: Claude Code · a demo vault, a made-up athlete

say: Before any numbers, two quick screening questions. Your answers decide what kind of eating plan I can safely set up.
1. **Have you ever had a hard time with food or eating?** …
2. **Has a clinician given you a diet, or is food part of managing a condition?** …
Thanks. Neither answer rules anything out, so you get the normal plan.
1. **How much do you want to count?**
- **Nothing** (hand portions and meal templates). This is the default.
- **Protein and calories**, from labels or an app.
4. **How's your appetite, and which meal of the day is hardest to get right?**

steps.user: 1: nothing, hand portions. … 4: good appetite; lunch at work is the hardest, I often grab whatever is there.

steps.note: ⋯ one more round: a normal day, foods and meal times ⋯

say: Protein · **131–180 g a day**, ticked at **131 g** · 1.6–2.2 g/kg for lifting goals at 82.0 kg (Morton 2018, Strong)
2. **Lunch from home.** You said lunch at work is the hardest meal and you often grab whatever's there. So cook double at dinner and box half.
12:30 · **Lunch** (the hardest meal) · Last night's dinner, boxed: 2 palms protein + the plate above (about 40–55 g)
16:00 · **Snack**: swap the crisps or chocolate · Greek yoghurt with fruit, 2 eggs and an apple, or milk and nuts (about 20–25 g)
Your eating plan is written, and Pahlavan's Food tab reads it with no errors.
**You're fully set up.** … Your first session is Tue 10 Nov, and your first letter comes on Sun 15 Nov (`/fitness-coach checkin`).
